title: Rafael and the Homecoming
premise: August Vasquez has spent three years holding his family together with careful hands and invisible seams, until a recipe card in his late grandmother's box leads him to the Vela, a hidden community of people who shed their assigned identities to survive. Drawn into their world, August discovers he can unmake labels — including the ones he's built for himself — but every transformation costs memory, and the Vela's enemies are closing in. When his youngest sister follows him through, August must choose between reclaiming the self he buried to keep his family safe and sacrificing it to buy them all a way home. In the end, he gives up his own name to seal the door behind them, returning as a stranger who slowly, painfully, becomes someone new — loved not for who he was, but who he chooses to be.
about_author: Sable Vane grew up translating for adults in three languages and writes stories about kids who carry too much. They live near the coast with an unruly garden and a recipe box of their own.

chapters.title: The Careful Boy
chapters.summary: August's POV. A night in the Vasquez household: school forms signed, dinner stretched, little sister Marisol's nightmare soothed while mom works doubles. August is competent, exhausted, and utterly without wants of his own. Emotional beat: love as labor, and the quiet ache of being needed instead of known.

chapters.title: Card 47
chapters.summary: August's POV. Sorting grandma Rosa's belongings, August finds a recipe card that reads like instructions for a person, not a dish: 'remove the label before folding.' Touching the ink, the kitchen dissolves. Emotional beat: wonder cracking open routine; grief for grandma sharpening into curiosity.

chapters.title: The Vela
chapters.summary: August's POV. He wakes in a lantern-lit market where people wear no names and trade memories as currency. A guide named Wren explains the rules: here you may set down any identity — but what you release doesn't come back whole. Emotional beat: vertigo and strange belonging.

chapters.title: What August Left at the Door
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Watching August hesitate at the threshold, Wren sees her younger self — the girl who traded away 'dutiful daughter' and never got it back. She warns him; he enters anyway. Emotional beat: mentor's fear disguised as irritation.

chapters.title: First Unmaking
chapters.summary: August's POV. In a ritual bath of candle-smoke, August sheds the label 'the responsible one' for one hour. Lighter than air, he laughs for the first time in years — then returns to find Marisol left alone because he was gone. Emotional beat: euphoria curdling into guilt.

chapters.title: Marisol Follows
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Ten years old and sharp-eyed, she tracked the impossible smells from August's jacket. She slips through using grandma's second card. The Vela accepts her before August can stop it. Emotional beat: terror and reluctant awe — his sister belongs here more than he does.

chapters.title: The Price List
chapters.summary: August's POV. To bring Marisol home safely, they need passage from the Ferryman, who trades in memories. August learns what three years of caretaking actually cost him: he cannot remember mom's face before dad left. Emotional beat: horror at what survival already took.

chapters.title: Wren's Ledger
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren reveals why she stays: she traded her real name long ago and can't leave — the door only opens for those who know themselves. She's been searching the memory-market for thirty years. Emotional beat: hopelessness worn smooth into duty.

chapters.title: Labels Off
chapters.summary: August's POV. At a Vela festival of unmasking, August meets Ilya, who carries no past at all and is free because of it. They talk until dawn about whether a self is a cage or a gift. Emotional beat: first tenderness; the terrifying possibility of being seen.

chapters.title: Mom Works Nights
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Back home, mom notices the gaps — August forgetting chores, Marisol humming songs she never learned. A near-disaster at school forces August to lie badly. Emotional beat: the two worlds bleeding; the cost of divided attention.

chapters.title: The Collectors
chapters.summary: August's POV. Masked figures arrive at the Vela harvesting loose identities — the ones people discarded carelessly. One collector wears a face August almost recognizes: a boy who vanished from his neighborhood years ago. Emotional beat: dread made personal.

chapters.title: Ilya's Bargain
chapters.summary: Ilya's POV. Ilya confesses: they were born in the Vela, assembled from spare memories, and have never had a self to lose. They offer to carry part of August's price if he'll help them steal one. Emotional beat: love offered by someone with nothing to give but themselves.

chapters.title: Grandma's Whole Recipe
chapters.summary: August's POV. Decoding all of Rosa's cards, August learns she founded the Vela's escape routes — and that the final card is a way out that requires a full, willing surrender of one true name. Rosa gave hers to get her children out. Emotional beat: understanding grandma at last; inheritance as burden and blessing.

chapters.title: Marisol Trades
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Impatient with August's stalling, Marisol sells a memory of their father to fund their passage. August finds her hollow-eyed and furious at his anger — it was hers to sell. Emotional beat: sibling rupture; the ethics of survival argued in tears.

chapters.title: The Ferryman's Offer
chapters.summary: August's POV. The Ferryman makes a private deal: the family's safe passage in exchange for everything August is — every memory of being their protector. He'd walk out a stranger to the people he saved. Emotional beat: the central choice laid bare; love against duty with the terms inverted.

chapters.title: Raid on the Vela
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. The Collectors breach the lantern-walls, hunting unanchored souls. Wren holds the gate; Ilya shields Marisol; August realizes the raid isn't random — the Ferryman sold them out. Emotional beat: chaos, sacrifice, betrayal compounding.

chapters.title: Wren's Name
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. In the burning archive, Wren finds her own name in a ledger fragment — and spends it instantly to hold the door open for the children fleeing. She smiles as she forgets herself. Emotional beat: tragic grace; the mentor's arc completing in fire.

chapters.title: The Choice
chapters.summary: August's POV. At the threshold with Marisol and Ilya, August must speak his true name to open Rosa's final route — or take the Ferryman's deal and keep nothing. He chooses neither: he speaks his name AND gives it, splitting himself, paying double. Emotional beat: climax; agency reclaimed at maximum cost.

chapters.title: Homecoming
chapters.summary: August's POV. He wakes in his own bed with no memory of the last month. Mom cries with relief; Marisol watches him with terrible knowledge she can't explain. Something in him is missing and something else is quietly growing. Emotional beat: bittersweet return; the price paid in silence.

chapters.title: Stranger at the Table
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Weeks pass. August is gentler, stranger, laughing at things he shouldn't find funny. Marisol tests him with half-remembered rituals; he responds without knowing why. Emotional beat: grief and hope braided together; love persisting past recognition.

chapters.title: The New Recipe
chapters.summary: August's POV. A blank card appears in Rosa's box in his own handwriting: 'To make a self: begin with what remains.' August remembers enough — a lantern, a laugh, someone whose hand fit his. He chooses to become whoever this is, on purpose. Emotional beat: rebirth as authorship.

chapters.title: Who Comes Home
chapters.summary: August's POV, closing with Ilya's knock at the door. Ilya found their stolen self and crossed over carrying Wren's forgotten name, kept safe. On the porch, August doesn't remember them — but says yes anyway. Emotional beat: resolution; found family reassembled around a boy brave enough to start again.
